title: Instructions beyond the Torah
content:
Instructions beyond the Torah

Laws, Commands, and Instructions — the whole Bible · Old Testament · New Testament · Instructions index · Beyond the Torah · Counting and classification guide

This page preserves twelve supplemental passage records within the Bible-wide Laws, Commands, and Instructions study. The Old Testament catalogue and New Testament catalogue now provide the main book-by-book routes. X labels identify selected supplemental records, not additional unique laws to add to another collection’s total.

Christ and the apostles

Browse all 105 Christ studies and 124 apostolic teachings. Their original quotations and verse anchors remain on the existing source pages. The Harmony adds parables, wisdom passages and further biblical context; it is a complementary study view.

  • The Harmony of Instruction — The Law Fulfilled
  • The Harmony of Instruction — Repent, Believe, Follow
  • The Harmony of Instruction — Love, Mercy and Forgiveness
  • The Harmony of Instruction — Prayer, Fasting and Giving

Selected additional instruction records

Original recipients, literary form and scope are recorded before any theological classification. Where a relationship to an earlier law has not been established here, the classification remains open. Historical instructions are preserved without treating them as universal commands.

X001 · Cross the Jordan with the people

Original Scripture: Joshua 1:2

Original recipient: Joshua and Israel. Record type: Historical commission.

This instruction concerns Joshua’s leadership and Israel’s entry into the land. It does not commission every believer to cross the Jordan or claim territory.

X002 · Keep and meditate on the law entrusted to Joshua

Original Scripture: Joshua 1:7–9

Original recipient: Joshua. Record type: Historical commission with continuing teaching.

Keep the charge to Joshua and the land promise in context. The passage teaches attentive obedience; its prosperity language is not an unconditional promise of wealth to every reader.

X003 · Prepare provisions for the crossing

Original Scripture: Joshua 1:10–11

Original recipient: Israel, through Joshua’s officers. Record type: Historical operational direction.

Joshua gives a practical instruction for a particular journey. This is recorded separately from God’s direct commission in verses 2–9.

X004 · Serve the Lord and remove foreign gods

Original Scripture: Joshua 24:14–24

Original recipient: Israel at the covenant assembly. Record type: Covenant exhortation; continuity review open.

Joshua calls Israel to exclusive allegiance. Read the renewed covenant and the people’s response before applying the passage; this entry is not an additional count of the Torah’s prohibition of idolatry.

X005 · Trust God without exalting your own wisdom

Original Scripture: Proverbs 3:5–7

Original recipient: The learner addressed as a son. Record type: Wisdom instruction; continuity review open.

The selected Greek-based reading preserves self-exaltation in verse 5 and a feminine pronoun in verse 6. The summary does not replace those details with wording from another edition.

X006 · Receive the Lord’s discipline

Original Scripture: Proverbs 3:11–12

Original recipient: The learner addressed as a son. Record type: Wisdom instruction; continuity review open.

The instruction concerns responding to God’s correction. Its divine-parent image must not be used as permission for human abuse.

X007 · Do good promptly when you can help

Original Scripture: Proverbs 3:27–28

Original recipient: The wisdom learner who has means to help. Record type: Wisdom instruction; continuity review open.

The practical condition matters: help when it is within your means. The passage rebukes needless delay in giving available help.

X008 · Do justice, love mercy and be ready to walk with God

Original Scripture: Micah 6:8

Original recipient: The human hearer within the case against Israel. Record type: Prophetic instruction; continuity review open.

The Saints Greek-based wording says “be ready to walk.” “Humbly” belongs to the comparison tradition and is not silently substituted into this summary.

X009 · Remember, repent and return to the first works

Original Scripture: Revelation 2:4–7

Original recipient: The addressed church in Ephesus. Record type: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context.

The call to repentance belongs to Christ’s message concerning abandoned first love. Hear the whole message, including the appeal to the churches in verse 7.

X010 · Remain faithful through suffering

Original Scripture: Revelation 2:10–11

Original recipient: The addressed church in Smyrna. Record type: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context.

Keep the particular warning about coming suffering beside the call to faithfulness. Do not turn the ten days into a universal timetable.

X011 · Become watchful, remember and repent

Original Scripture: Revelation 3:2–3

Original recipient: The addressed church in Sardis. Record type: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context.

Christ’s rebuke concerns the church’s condition and incomplete works. This call is retained with its named audience rather than counted as three new universal laws.

X012 · Worship God

Original Scripture: Revelation 22:8–9

Original recipient: John, corrected by the angel. Record type: Direct instruction; continuity review open.

The angel refuses John’s worship and directs him to God. This concerns the object of worship; the messenger’s role does not make the messenger divine.

How wider coverage is assessed

  • Read the entire chapter and record who speaks, to whom, and in what circumstances.
  • Identify duties, prohibitions and commissions; keep promises, narrative, doctrine and wisdom forms distinguishable.
  • Link repetition to an existing record before adding a new requirement. Retain parallel Gospel wording and Greek/English numbering differences.
  • Assign Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged or Everlasting only with explicit supporting passages and a stated scope. Historical setting and interpretive uncertainty remain visible.
